title: Superseded playback attempts keep mutating shared refs and the video element after awaits
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a relay start superseded by a socket reconnect leaves no stale playback, error or subscription' (chromium); tests/subscriptionLedger.test.js (VAL-156): "a stale attempt's late acknowledgement after a newer start sends no relay-consume-stop", 'a stale attempt that is still the latest claimant on the same socket sends exactly one stop', 'no stop after the socket reconnected under a new socket.id', 'no stop while the socket is disconnected, and no start either', 'a committed subscription is stopped once, by cleanupPlayback, and never again by its attempt', 'the claim is recorded in the same synchronous block as the start emit', 'a start acknowledgement times out once, and a late answer is ignored', 'canRelease and release act only on the latest claim of the same kind', 'WatchView and its session controller send relay starts and stops only through the ledger'; tests/playbackAttempt.test.js: stale detection, identifiable superseded error, own-resource disposal, current-attempt pass-through, and four recovery-guard tests (drop, coalesced follow-up with the chain intent, clearFollowUp and a failing recovery, re-entrant trigger)
proof: Browser repro (the issue's socket-reconnect trigger): a tunnel-origin viewer clicks Watch; the test holds back the viewer's live media-init frames, so the relay-first attempt waits in its 7 s live media-init wait; the test then closes the viewer's WebSocket and socket.io-client reconnects under a new socket.id, so onReconnect runs cleanupPlayback and rejoins. On the unchanged code (vite build of HEAD c7489d0, server.js on 3210 under the Playwright lock) the test failed at 'getByText(/WebRTC mode active|relay mode active/i) toHaveCount(0)': received 1. The trace shows that about 7 s after the reconnect the superseded attempt rejected with 'Relay stream is not ready yet', and the handleWatch call started before the reconnect ran cleanupPlayback and its WebRTC fallback ('Trying mediasoup fallback', 'Mediasoup fallback connected', status 'WebRTC mode active (lowest latency).') in the reconnected session, with no click. After the fix it passes: no alert, no playback mode, room viewerCount 1 / relayViewerCount 0 / mediasoupConsumerCount 0, video src '' and no srcObject, Watch Stream enabled, and a new Watch plays through the relay with relayViewerCount 1. It passed 3 of 3 with --repeat-each=3, and the whole media-flow spec passes 13 of 13. The unit tests cannot run on the unchanged code (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the new modules); the source-level ledger test failed there with 'WatchView.jsx must not emit relay-consume-start/stop directly'. Fix: src/lib/playbackAttempt.mjs (SupersededAttemptError, isSupersededAttemptError, assertAttemptCurrent, beginPlaybackAttempt with own/dispose/settleFailure, createRecoveryGuard); src/lib/subscriptionLedger.mjs (claim/canRelease/release; emitClaimedStart claims in the same synchronous block as the emit and refuses while disconnected; releaseSubscription emits the stop only when canRelease holds). WatchView checks the attempt after every await in startMediasoupPlayback, consumeProducer and startRelayPlayback before shared writes; a stale attempt closes its own transport or consumer and revokes its own object URL; handleWatch, onTransportFailed, onReconnect and handleTryMediasoup return on a superseded rejection; useViewerSessionController's relay-subscription owner releases the committed claim through the ledger; transport-failed and reconnect share one recovery guard. Verification: node --test of the two new files 17/17; eslint of the four files clean; npm run lint and typecheck clean; npm test 1097/1097. Outputs in the lane scratchpad: watch-TASK-087-before.txt, watch-TASK-087-unit-before.txt, watch-TASK-087-after-media-flow.txt, watch-TASK-087-after-repeat.txt, watch-TASK-087-npmtest.txt.
